speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the shooting ear pain you're experiencing, such as when it started and what makes it better or worse? Also, how long ago was your tympanoplasty performed?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain started shortly after my surgery, which was 12 weeks ago, and it feels like a sharp shock specifically when I chew or swallow. It hasn't really improved, and I also feel a dull discomfort whenever I try to wear earrings in that ear. However, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the sharp pain triggered by chewing and swallowing shortly after tympanoplasty, I suspect involvement of the facial nerve or the tensor tympani muscle, but the earring discomfort suggests a local issue. Let me examine your ear canal and tympanic membrane to check for granulation tissue, cholesteatoma recurrence, or hardware irritation. REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the otoscopy is normal, I suspect the pain is neuropathic, possibly involving the auriculotemporal nerve or the facial nerve due to surgical trauma. Do you experience any facial weakness, changes in taste, or pain that radiates to your jaw or temple when you chew?

speaker: Patient
text: I don't have any facial weakness or changes in taste, but the pain does seem to radiate toward my jaw when I eat. I’ve also been dealing with a lot of stress from work and poor sleep, which might be making it feel worse. I want to emphasize that, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor
text: The radiation of pain to the jaw during chewing, combined with the history of recent ear surgery, strongly suggests irritation or injury to the auriculotemporal nerve or the temporomandibular joint. I will order a CT scan of the temporal bone to rule out any bony abnormalities or hardware issues near the mandibular condyle. REQUEST TEST: CT_Temporal_Bone

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the normal imaging and the specific trigger of pain during chewing radiating to the jaw, I suspect this is temporomandibular joint dysfunction or auriculotemporal neuralgia exacerbated by post-surgical scarring. Does pressing on the area just in front of your ear, near the jaw joint, reproduce the shooting pain?

REQUEST TEST: TMJ_MRI

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the imaging is normal and the pain is triggered by chewing and earring pressure, I suspect Auriculotemporal Neuralgia or post-surgical scar tissue entrapment. Do you have any history of herpes zoster (shingles) in that area, and does applying a cold compress to the side of your face provide any relief?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have never had shingles in that area. Applying a cold compress doesn't seem to help much, but the pain is definitely still there.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal imaging and the specific trigger of pain with chewing and earring pressure, I suspect Auriculotemporal Neuralgia or post-surgical scar tissue entrapment. To confirm if this is neuropathic pain, does applying a topical lidocaine patch to the ear area provide any temporary relief?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't tried a lidocaine patch yet, but the pain is quite sharp and localized. I can certainly give that a try before our next appointment to see if it helps.

speaker: Doctor
text: Please try the lidocaine patch and let me know if it provides any relief, as this will help confirm if the pain is neuropathic. Also, does pressing on the tragus or the area just in front of the ear canal reproduce the shooting pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, pressing on the area just in front of my ear canal definitely triggers that sharp, shooting pain. I haven't had a chance to try the lidocaine patch yet since we just started this conversation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The tenderness just anterior to the ear canal and pain triggered by chewing strongly point to auriculotemporal neuralgia, likely caused by scar tissue entrapping the nerve during your recent tympanoplasty. Since imaging is normal and the clinical signs align with nerve irritation, I am confident in this diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia
